<style>
/* Bigger, black legend text for every Observable Plot chart on this page.
   Plot renders its color-swatch legend as a separate HTML block (not SVG)
   with a hardcoded 10px font, so it needs its own override here -- the
   axis/tick/title font size and color are set per-chart instead, via each
   Plot.plot()'s `style` option below. */
[class*="-swatches"] {
  font-size: 15px !important;
  color: black !important;
}

/* Filter row (Cohort/Region/LEA/School + the Total Schools tile): each
   control only takes the width it needs instead of being stretched into
   an equal-width grid column, so they sit close together instead of
   spread across the full page width. Wraps as needed on narrower
   screens/content columns; the Total Schools tile is pushed to the end
   of whichever line it lands on (margin-left: auto). */
.filter-row {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: flex-end;
  column-gap: 28px;
  row-gap: 14px;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
}
.filter-row > .cell {
  flex: 0 0 auto;
}
/* The Total Schools tile (last item) always gets its own line, right-
   aligned, instead of sharing a line with whichever filter wrapped down
   next to it -- cleaner than the two fighting over vertical alignment
   when their heights differ. */
.filter-row > .cell:last-child {
  flex: 1 0 100%;
  display: flex;
  justify-content: flex-end;
  margin-top: 6px;
}
/* Each Inputs.select renders as its own <form>, and Observable's Inputs
   library gives that form a built-in ~360px default width (sized for
   standalone notebook use) with the label and select splitting that
   width evenly -- that, not the grid layout, was the real source of the
   big gaps. Override it here so each control is only as wide as its
   label + its options need. The School list has some long "name (LEA)"
   entries, so its select gets a max-width with ellipsis truncation in
   the closed state; the full text still shows when the list is open. */
.filter-row form {
  width: auto !important;
  max-width: none !important;
}
.filter-row form label {
  width: auto !important;
  margin-right: 8px;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
.filter-row form select {
  width: auto !important;
  max-width: 240px;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
</style>

# Is school climate improving as grantees implement the CCSPP?

## Overview of *School Climate* in Year 3 - Quantitative Analysis
:::

The APR has a few questions that ask whether grantees are collecting data on school climate and whether they see it improving under the community schools strategy. School climate covers how safe, supportive and connected a school feels to students, families and staff. It's a key sign of whether the community schools approach is changing how schools work day to day.


**Instructions:** Select a CCSPP Cohort, Region, Local Educational Agency (LEA), and/or School below to filter every chart on this page. Hover over any bar for details.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

source("00-prepare-climate-data.R")

ojs_define(
  climate_data_bridge = school_climate_long,
  phase_defs_bridge    = phase_definitions
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
data = transpose(climate_data_bridge)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
definitions = transpose(phase_defs_bridge)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cohortOptions = [...new Set(data.map(d => d.cohort))].sort()
```

```{ojs}

```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
leaOptions = [...new Set(data.map(d => d.lea))].sort()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false

```

::: filter-row
```{ojs}

```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof regionFilter = Inputs.select(["All", ...regionOptions], {label: "Region:"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof leaFilter = Inputs.select(["All", ...leaOptions], {label: "LEA:"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Only offers schools that match the Cohort/Region/LEA filters already
// picked above, so this list narrows as those are set; changing any of
// those three resets this dropdown back to "All" (a fresh Inputs.select
// is created whenever schoolOptions recomputes). Options are keyed by the
// school's CDS code, not its name -- several schools statewide share the
// same name (e.g. "Lincoln Elementary" appears in 14 different LEAs), so
// name alone isn't a safe filter key; the LEA is shown alongside the name
// to tell same-named schools apart in the list.
viewof schoolFilter = Inputs.select(["All", ...schoolOptions], {
  label: "School:",
  format: d => d === "All" ? "All" : `${d.school_name} (${d.lea})`
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div style="border:1px solid #ddd; border-radius:6px; padding:8px 14px; text-align:center;">
  <div style="font-size:0.8rem; color:#27475C; font-weight:bold;">Total Schools</div>
  <div style="font-size:1.8rem; font-weight:bold; color:#005DAA;">${filteredSchools.length}</div>
</div>`
```
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
schoolOptions = {
  const rows = data.filter(d =>
    (cohortFilter === "All" || d.cohort === cohortFilter) &&
    (regionFilter === "All" || d.region === regionFilter) &&
    (leaFilter === "All" || d.lea === leaFilter)
  );
  const uniq = new Map();
  for (const d of rows) {
    if (!uniq.has(d.cds_code)) {
      uniq.set(d.cds_code, { cds_code: d.cds_code, school_name: d.school_name, lea: d.lea });
    }
  }
  return Array.from(uniq.values()).sort((a, b) =>
    a.school_name.localeCompare(b.school_name) || a.lea.localeCompare(b.lea)
  );
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
filteredLong = data.filter(d =>
  (cohortFilter === "All" || d.cohort === cohortFilter) &&
  (regionFilter === "All" || d.region === regionFilter) &&
  (leaFilter === "All" || d.lea === leaFilter) &&
  (schoolFilter === "All" || d.cds_code === schoolFilter.cds_code)
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// climate fields repeat identically across a school's 5 strategy-rows, so
// dedupe back to one row per school for anything that isn't strategy-specific
filteredSchools = filteredLong.filter(d => d.strategy === strategyKeys[0])
```

## School Climate Measure

### Does your school currently collect data and track progress on school climate?

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
q137Agg = {
  const rows = filteredSchools.filter(d => d.climate_tracks_data);
  const groups = d3.rollup(rows, v => v.length, d => d.climate_tracks_data);
  const total = d3.sum(Array.from(groups.values()));
  return ["Yes", "No"].map(k => ({
    category: "All Schools", key: k,
    n: groups.get(k) ?? 0,
    pct: total > 0 ? (groups.get(k) ?? 0) / total : 0
  }));
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Two-point scale: first 2 colors from the shared blue scale (darkest -> lightest)
q137Color = ({ Yes: "#346FAB", No: "#AACCE9" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 20,
  marginBottom: 50,
  width: width,
  height: 150,
  style: { fontSize: "15px", color: "black" },
  x: { percent: true, label: "% of Respondents", labelAnchor: "center" },
  y: { axis: null },
  color: { domain: ["Yes", "No"], range: ["Yes", "No"].map(k => q137Color[k]), legend: true },
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(q137Agg, Plot.stackX({
      x: "pct", y: "category", fill: "key",
      title: d => `Tracks school climate data: ${d.key}\n% of Respondents: ${(d.pct * 100).toFixed(0)}%\nn = ${d.n}`
    })),
    Plot.text(q137Agg, Plot.stackX({
      x: "pct", y: "category",
      text: d => d.pct >= 0.04 ? `${(d.pct * 100).toFixed(0)}%` : "",
      fill: "white", fontWeight: "bold"
    })),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

## Capacity-Building Strategies: Phase of Growth vs. School Climate

Pick a strategy below to see how a school's phase of growth on that particular strategy relates to the two school climate measures above.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Rows: Visioning / Engaging / Transforming / Null (no response)
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
phaseOrder = ["Visioning", "Engaging", "Transforming", "Null"]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof cbsStrategyFilter = Inputs.select(strategyKeys, { label: "CBS Strategy:", value: strategyKeys[0] })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cbsScopedLong = filteredLong.filter(d => d.strategy === cbsStrategyFilter)
```

### Does your school currently collect data and track progress on school climate?

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Same 2-blue scale used for the Yes/No chart above, kept as its own copy
// here so this section doesn't depend on a cell defined earlier in the page.
cbsTrackColor = ({ Yes: "#346FAB", No: "#AACCE9" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cbsTrackAgg = {
  const rows = cbsScopedLong.filter(d => d.climate_tracks_data);
  const groups = d3.rollup(rows, v => v.length, d => d.phase, d => d.climate_tracks_data);
  const result = [];
  for (const phase of phaseOrder) {
    const respMap = groups.get(phase) ?? new Map();
    const total = d3.sum(Array.from(respMap.values()));
    for (const response of ["Yes", "No"]) {
      const n = respMap.get(response) ?? 0;
      const pct = total > 0 ? n / total : 0;
      result.push({ phase, response, n, total, pct });
    }
  }
  return result;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 120,
  marginBottom: 50,
  width: width,
  height: 260,
  style: { fontSize: "15px", color: "black" },
  x: { percent: true, label: "% of Respondents", labelAnchor: "center" },
  y: { label: null, domain: phaseOrder },
  color: { domain: ["Yes", "No"], range: ["Yes", "No"].map(k => cbsTrackColor[k]), legend: true },
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(cbsTrackAgg, Plot.stackX({
      x: "pct", y: "phase", fill: "response",
      title: d => `${cbsStrategyFilter}\n` +
                   `Phase of Growth and Development: ${d.phase}\n` +
                   `Tracks school climate data: ${d.response}\n` +
                   `% of Respondents: ${(d.pct * 100).toFixed(0)}%\nn = ${d.n}`
    })),
    Plot.text(cbsTrackAgg, Plot.stackX({
      x: "pct", y: "phase",
      text: d => d.pct >= 0.06 ? `${(d.pct * 100).toFixed(0)}%` : "",
      fill: "white", fontWeight: "bold"
    })),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

### Our school climate has improved since we started implementing the CCSPP

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cbsResponseOrder = ["Strongly disagree", "Somewhat disagree", "Neither agree nor disagree", "Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree"]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Same 5-point scale used for the "Our school climate has improved" chart
// above, kept as its own copy here so this section doesn't depend on a cell
// defined earlier in the page.
cbsClimateColor = ({
  "Strongly disagree": "#C55A11",
  "Somewhat disagree": "#F4B183",
  "Neither agree nor disagree": "#9DC3E6",
  "Somewhat agree": "#2E75B6",
  "Strongly agree": "#1F4E79"
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cbsClimateAgg = {
  const rows = cbsScopedLong.filter(d => d.climate_improved);
  const groups = d3.rollup(rows, v => v.length, d => d.phase, d => d.climate_improved);
  const result = [];
  for (const phase of phaseOrder) {
    const respMap = groups.get(phase) ?? new Map();
    const total = d3.sum(Array.from(respMap.values()));
    for (const response of cbsResponseOrder) {
      const n = respMap.get(response) ?? 0;
      const pct = total > 0 ? n / total : 0;
      result.push({ phase, response, n, total, pct });
    }
  }
  return result;
}
```
